text: yeah or i would start with trees. they seem to be the most problematic of the bunch so the hardest hitter would be nice to see up front
resolution: Shrank the palm-frond instance from 80B to 24B (3.33x) — the hardest-hitting foliage. New FrondInstance (pos f32x3, pitch/yaw u16x2, wide/len unorm16x2, rgb unorm8x4) replaces the full 80-byte model matrix; frond_wgsl rebuilds the matrix from TRS (rz dropped, sx==sz folded) and derives the per-frond spaghetti seed from the rebuilt columns so the look is preserved. Fronds also moved to a dedicated GPU buffer (g_frond_static_buf ~24MB + per-frame g_frond_inst_buf) off the shared 1.05M static pool, so a palm-heavy view no longer starves buildings/grass. Isolated to the existing ~frond~ pipeline; buildings/grass/water untouched. Both editor (v8_app) and no-V8 loader compile + render green (63k instances, zero GPU-validation errors). Visual confirmation of trees pending user eyeball via rjit game play. Known follow-up: setupStreaming still counts frond rows against MAX_STATIC_INSTANCES so lod_budget stays 0 on big maps — decoupling that is the next step to fully kill the in-view despawn.
